message: In the concealed twin Tuned Mass Damper (TMD, mass on spring with damper tuned to bridge mode) retrofit concept, the clamp-beam static load path has slip and sag risk raised by Manager, thank you Manager. To check it I used hand calculation (the unit weight calculation (E10) and the clamp-beam moment calculation (E12) with the beam stress check (E14)). I found 2452.5 newtons per 250 kilogram unit with 1103.6 newton-metres moment and 16.5 megapascals stress on Square Hollow Section (SHS, square steel tube) 100 by 6 millimetre beams, and 75.9 millimetres static sag (the spring sag estimate (E11)) plus 20.0 millimetres travel (the two-degree-of-freedom response simulation (E6)), according to Den Hartog, 1934. I propose transverse SHS clamp beams U-bolted with four Metric 20 (M20, 20 millimetre diameter) U-bolts per beam to existing cross-girders below the soffit with 150 millimetre clearance envelope and deck-matching soffit paint. In the same concealed mounting concept, thank you Structural Dynamics Lead and Vibration Control Specialist, the deck sightline method has visibility risk. To check it I used the concealed mounting detail (the concealed mounting detail sketch (E9)) with the under-deck twin-unit layout (the under-deck twin-unit layout sketch (E7)). I found zero hardware above deck level with paired units hung below girders and access by soffit hatches, according to Setra, 2006. I propose no change to the under-deck layout with removable parapet-void covers for re-tuning. My position: ready because deck-view preservation and maintainable under-deck connection fidelity are shown.
